title.narrative: Food Systems Transformation in Usangu Landscape

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
To catalyze the transformation to sustainable rice-livestock-aquaculture food systems that are nature positive, resilient, and pollution-reduced.

Transforming food systems will deliver significant socioeconomic benefits to smallholder producers, SMEs and rural communities. The project will directly benefit 149,325 women, men and youth, through investments in profitable and sustainable production and business models. Investments in sustainable and efficient production practices and technologies across rice, livestock, aquaculture and associated value chains will increase productivity and reduce post-harvest and financial losses for smallholder farmers. Tackling inequalities is key to sustainable development, therefore the project will elevate the position of women and youth in the agricultural value chain through active participation and decision making at various scales. The project’s diversification strategy will contribute to improved nutrition and resilience, protecting farmers from climate risks such as drought that often wipe off harvests. In improving the financial and organization capacities of smallholder farmers, the project will improve business skills rural populations and elevate their earning through agriculture as a decent source of employment. In addition, the protection of catchment areas including wetlands will sustain water to the important biodiversity areas, such as Ruaha National Park, that generate considerable tourism revenue and contribution to Tanzania’s economy.
